The proposed strategy employs simulated annealing (SA) to escape local minima and explore the solution space globally. SA iteratively accepts both improving and worsening solutions with decreasing probability, guided by an annealing schedule. This approach addresses the challenge of the non-convex overlap integral objective by allowing exploration of alternative optima while maintaining solution feasibility.

**Decision variable**: \( h \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\text{points}}} \), \( h[i] \in [0,1] \)  
**Objective**: Minimize \( C_5 = \max_k \left( \sum_{x=0}^{n_{\text{points}}-1} h(x)(1 - h(x+k)) \cdot dx \right) \)  
**Constraints**:  
1. \( \sum_{i=0}^{n_{\text{points}}-1} h[i] = \frac{n_{\text{points}}}{2} \)  
2. \( 0 \leq h[i] \leq 1 \)
